hooks.text: Undocking to escape a spinning spacecraft made Gemini 8 spin even faster.
Neil Armstrong nearly blacked out when his capsule spun at one revolution per second.
Seventy-five percent of reentry fuel was burned just to stop a lethal capsule spin.

title: When Neil Armstrong's capsule spun out of control
description: Neil Armstrong's first spaceflight nearly ended in disaster when Gemini 8 suffered a stuck thruster in orbit.

beats.text: Command pilot Neil Armstrong and pilot David Scott launched aboard Gemini 8 on March 16, 1966.
beats.visual: photograph of launch of Gemini 8 on Titan II rocket, Cape Canaveral, 1966

beats.text: The mission successfully achieved the world's first orbital docking with an Agena target vehicle.
beats.visual: photograph of Gemini Agena Target Vehicle in orbit seen from Gemini 8, 1966
queries: Gemini Agena Target Vehicle orbit Gemini 8

beats.text: Minutes later, a short-circuited thruster threw the joined spacecraft into an uncontrollable roll.
beats.visual: photograph of Gemini spacecraft cockpit instrument panel, 1966

beats.text: Believing the target vehicle was malfunctioning, the crew undocked while out of radio range.
beats.visual: photograph of Gemini 8 docking nose-to-nose with Agena, 1966

beats.text: Without the Agena's mass, the capsule accelerated to nearly one revolution per second.
beats.visual: photograph of Gemini 8 mission insignia patch, 1966

beats.text: Armstrong fired the reentry thrusters to halt the tumble, consuming seventy-five percent of their maneuvering fuel.
beats.visual: photograph of Gemini 8 capsule in water with flotation collar and pararescuers, 1966

beats.text: Safety rules forced an emergency splashdown in the western Pacific Ocean.
beats.visual: photograph of Gemini 8 spacecraft being hoisted aboard recovery ship USS Leonard F. Mason, 1966
